title: William Lilly 1647 first edition printed CHAP CX / editorial CXI — Stature, Form and Shape of Body
provenance: Wellcome original b30338724 IIIF original page images, source PDF frames 580-582
source_quality: Original 1647 scanned images visually examined. Selective source anchors, not a full diplomatic transcription.
format_notes: PDF580/581 printed folios appear as 538/539 after frame579 printed545; body order continuous, PDF582 resumes expected numeral548. Do not reorder the pages.
inference_status: Historical untested physical-appearance/stature hypotheses. No prediction of actual heights, ethnic appearance, illness or disability; no runtime promotion.

groups.source_group: Stature chapter heading and priority rule

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CX Of the Stature, Forme, or shape of the Body
claims.meaning_historical_only: Printed chapter CX (editorial CXI) begins on PDF580 below the divider, after the prior intellect chapter.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: that Planet who doth partilly behold the Lord of the ascendant
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly derives alleged tall versus short stature primarily from a planet in a partile aspect to the Lord of Ascendant.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if many doe behold him, then judge from the strongest
claims.meaning_historical_only: When multiple planets aspect the Ascendant ruler, he says to judge stature using the strongest rather than treating all factors equally.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn Orientall A moderate stature declining rather to brevity
claims.meaning_historical_only: Oriental Saturn is said to indicate medium height tending toward shorter stature.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn Occidentall A short stature
claims.meaning_historical_only: Occidental Saturn is alleged to indicate short stature.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter Orientall A goodly tall stature
claims.meaning_historical_only: Oriental Jupiter is alleged to indicate tall stature.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter Occidentall Of moderate stature but inclining to tallness
claims.meaning_historical_only: Occidental Jupiter is alleged to indicate medium-to-tall stature, not simply short.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mars Orientall Tall Stature
claims.meaning_historical_only: Oriental Mars is alleged to indicate tall stature.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mars Occidentall Moderate in height but more long then short
claims.meaning_historical_only: Occidental Mars is alleged to indicate middle height inclining taller than shorter.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus Orientall One more tall and slender
claims.meaning_historical_only: Oriental Venus is alleged to indicate taller and slender build, not height alone.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus Occidentall Of more short stature inclining to brevity
claims.meaning_historical_only: Occidental Venus is alleged to indicate shorter stature.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury Orientall One of middle stature but verging to height
claims.meaning_historical_only: Oriental Mercury is alleged to signify average height trending taller.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury Occidentall Of small stature or but moderately tall
claims.meaning_historical_only: Occidental Mercury is said to indicate smaller or moderately tall stature, a deliberately broad outcome.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury whether he be Orientall or Occidentall ... Dispositor
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly explicitly states Mercury's dispositor modifies body/stature irrespective of oriental versus occidental status.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury in his owne house
claims.meaning_historical_only: Mercury in its own domicile is treated as a case where the sign determines stature rather than an orientation table alone.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury in the Suns house
claims.meaning_historical_only: Mercury in a house of the Sun is treated as a sign-based stature-modification case.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Mercury in the Moon her house
claims.meaning_historical_only: Mercury in a house of the Moon is separately named as a sign-based stature-modification case.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: The same course the Luminaries observe
claims.meaning_historical_only: The Sun and Moon are said to follow an analogous stature-disposition rule, without full quantitative thresholds.

groups.source_group: Proportion of members procedure crossing physical page seam

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Of the proportion of the Members
claims.meaning_historical_only: A separate subsection considers overall bodily shape rather than height alone.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the Signe ascending and his Lord
claims.meaning_historical_only: Body form is to be considered from the rising sign and its ruler; this is not identical to the stature-planet tie-breaker.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the Planet or Planets in the ascendant or affecting it
claims.meaning_historical_only: Lilly includes planets in the first house and planets forming aspects to the ascendant as distinct sources.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the two Lights viz Sun and Moon
claims.meaning_historical_only: Both solar and lunar placements are separate testimonies in the author's body-proportion method.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the season of the yeer
claims.meaning_historical_only: The calendar season is listed among alleged modifiers of proportions, and must not be confused with birth-year cohort effects.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: fixed Starres in the ascendant or neer the cusp thereof
claims.meaning_historical_only: Fixed stars near the ascendant cusp are a further original source condition; no numerical orb is supplied here.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXI Nature of the Signes Colour of the Face and Haire
claims.meaning_historical_only: The next numbered printed chapter begins below the original divider in frame PDF581; its sign/colour/appearance rules are NOT extracted in this batch.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: This is sufficiently handled in our Introduction or first Part from pag 93 to 99
claims.meaning_historical_only: The following chapter explicitly cross-references Book I pages 93–99; do not count this cross-reference as a validated stature outcome.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Yet briefly ... twelve sign stature categories
claims.meaning_historical_only: The following printed sign-height categories are reserved for the next batch rather than silently pooled with planetary stature in the current chapter.
